subject: Data tenure and erasure: hosted API — LumenBridge security questionnaire
messages:
From: Evan Clarke <evan.clarke@lumenbridge.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: LumenBridge Security Team <security@lumenbridge.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: LumenBridge questionnaire: data retention / deletion for hosted API

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this. We're completing our vendor security questionnaire and have a short section on data tenure and deletion for hosted APIs. Can you confirm the following for Redwood's hosted offering? We're primarily concerned about customer-generated prompts/responses, debug/request logs, backups/snapshots, and any ephemeral caches used by the runtime. Specific Qs: 

1) What is the default retention period for request payloads (prompts) and generated responses in the hosted API? Is that window configurable per account?
2) Are request/response records and debug logs included in backups/snapshots? If so, how long are backups retained and in what regions?
3) If we request a full account erasure, what steps do you take to delete customer data from live systems, caches, backups, and logs? Please include estimated timelines for each subsystem.
4) Do you provide a programmatic erasure API or webhook that we can call to automate tenant deletion? If not, what's the manual process and SLA?
5) Does Redwood retain any customer content for debugging or quality monitoring beyond the retention window? If yes, how is that access governed and audited?
6) We require proof-of-deletion (a signed statement or export). Do you provide deletion attestations for account terminations?

I've attached the LumenBridge questionnaire (first tab) with the specific wording we need answered. Would like to get this back by end of week if possible.

Best,
Evan
Evan Clarke
Senior Security Manager | LumenBridge

Attachments: lumenbridge_data_questions.xlsx (spreadsheet with vendor questions)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: LumenBridge questionnaire: data retention / deletion for hosted API

Hi Evan — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers mapped to your numbered items; I kept the wording pragmatic so you can paste directly into the questionnaire. If you'd like, we can do a short technical call to walk through any of these points.

1) Default retention for prompts/responses: We retain request payloads and generated responses for 30 days by default for hosted API customers. Accounts can opt into shorter retention windows (down to 0 days) via support request for an additional compliance configuration.

2) Backups/snapshots: Persistent backups (service metadata and configuration) are retained for 90 days. We do not include live request/response bodies in long-term, multi-day backups by default — those are treated as live telemetry and subject to the 30-day retention above. Short-lived runtime snapshots used for debugging may contain transient request metadata (not full payloads) and are retained for a maximum of 7 days. Backups are kept in the region(s) where the tenant's primary data resides; we can provide a region map on request.

3) Account erasure steps & timelines:
  - Live systems (storage buckets, logs index): we delete tenant records within 48 hours of an approved erasure request.
  - Runtime caches / KV caches: ephemeral caches are flushed immediately; deletion confirmation in logs within 24 hours.
  - Debug logs / request traces: removed from index within 48 hours; any aggregated anonymized telemetry retained for product analytics is separated and cannot be reconnected to tenant identifiers.
  - Backups/snapshots: tiered purge — short-term snapshots cleared within 7–14 days; deeper persistent backups purged within 90 days (we mark the tenant data for deletion immediately and it is excluded from restores).

4) Programmatic erasure: We provide a tenant deletion API for Dedicated and Private customers; for hosted API customers we currently offer a documented support-driven API endpoint (POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/erase) that we execute with a 48-hour SLA for completion. Roadmap includes self-service erase for hosted tenants; ETA depends on customer demand.

5) Retention for debugging/quality: We may retain short-lived copies of request metadata for debugging up to 7 days as noted above. We do not retain full prompts/responses longer than the configured retention window unless a customer explicitly opts in for debugging retention. Access to debugging copies is restricted to authorized engineers and is audited via our access logs and ticket trace.

6) Proof-of-deletion: We provide a deletion attestation document once the purge completes (signed PDF with deletion timestamps and a list of systems affected). For large enterprise contracts we can include this as part of termination paperwork.

I've attached a diagram of our deletion flow for clarity and included links to our internal playbook. Let me know if any of these need stronger SLA language and I can loop in Legal/Security for wording.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Security & Compliance Liaison | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_deletion_flow_diagram.png

From: Evan Clarke <evan.clarke@lumenbridge.com>

Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: LumenBridge questionnaire: data retention / deletion for hosted API

Hi Kimberly — this is very helpful, thanks. A couple of follow-ups before we finalize wording in the questionnaire: 

- Can you confirm whether the 30-day default includes request/response bodies that are stored in temporary queues during streaming sessions? LumenBridge uses streaming a lot and needs assurance those payloads are covered.

- For backups: you said "not include live request/response bodies in long-term backups by default" — can you confirm whether any automated disaster-recovery snapshots capture complete request bodies? We need to make sure there are no hidden longer-lived copies.

- The programmatic erasure path for hosted: you noted it's support-driven. For our procurement checklist we need either a self-service API or documented escalation + SLA that guarantees completion in 48 hours. Can Redwood include a binding 48-hour SLA for hosted account erasure execution?

- For the attestation: can Redwood provide a machine-readable deletion manifest (JSON) with timestamps and system identifiers in addition to the signed PDF? That would help automate our audit ingestion.

If you can confirm these points, we should be able to close out this section.

Regards,
Evan

On the attachment: we've included a short checklist; happy to accept your language if it maps directly into our questionnaire cells.

Hannah / Rishi — forwarding Evan's follow-ups (below). Can you review the three ask areas and confirm final wording we can commit to: 1) streaming payload coverage, 2) backups/DR snapshot guarantee, 3) whether Legal can sign a 48-hour SLA for hosted erasures and whether we can attach a JSON manifest as part of attestation.

My suggested answers:
- Streaming payloads: covered by the 30-day retention and treated as request bodies; ephemeral streaming queues are purged immediately after session end and are captured only as transient logs (max 7 days).
- Backups/DR: commit that standard DR snapshots do not include full request/response bodies; we will exclude request/response bodies from any snapshot that is retained beyond 7 days.
- Erasure SLA: we can commit to a 48-hour execution SLA for hosted erasure requests performed via our documented support-driven API; Legal to confirm wording and whether a financial or credit remedy is required for SLA failure.
- Attestation: we can provide both signed PDF and a machine-readable JSON manifest listing deleted systems and timestamps.

Please reply with edits and mark OK if we can send this as Redwood's formal response to LumenBridge.

Thanks — kim

Hi Evan and team — thanks for the follow-ups and for the patience while we confirmed internal wording. Below is the finalized language you can put into the questionnaire cells. I've attached the deletion-flow diagram and the machine-readable deletion manifest schema for your auditors.

Streaming payloads: Confirmed. All streaming requests and generated responses are treated as request/response bodies and fall under the same retention policy (30 days default). Runtime streaming queues are ephemeral and flushed at session end; any transient logs that capture streaming metadata are retained for up to 7 days and do not contain full payload bodies by default.

Backups & DR snapshots: Confirmed. Our standard DR snapshots and long-term backups do not include customer request/response bodies. Any snapshot that might capture request metadata is retained no longer than 7 days; persistent backups retained for 90 days are limited to service metadata and configuration and are excluded from request/response content. We will include an explicit exclusion rule for request/response bodies in our DR runbooks for LumenBridge.

Erasure execution SLA & process: For hosted API customers we will execute erasure requests submitted via our documented support-driven API endpoint. Redwood commits to execution of the deletion workflow within 48 hours of validation of the request (validation includes authentication and verification of authorized requester). The workflow covers live storage, index deletion, cache flushes, and marking backups for purge. Financial remedies for SLA breaches are handled per contract; please flag if you require specific credits in your procurement terms.

Proof-of-deletion: We will provide both a signed PDF attestation and a machine-readable JSON deletion manifest that lists deleted system identifiers and ISO timestamps. The manifest schema and an example are attached.

Next steps: I've attached two files for your review — our deletion flow diagram and an example JSON manifest. If that maps to your questionnaire wording, we're good to close this section. If you want legal to sign an addendum that embeds the 48-hour SLA into the MSA, we can route that separately.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
